verdict.rationale: Smooth's session API lets a developer send natural-language `run_task` steps and break workflows into smaller steps within a persistent browser. This approximates an `act` primitive on described intent, but there are no documented granular click/type primitives targeting described elements. Resilience to selector or layout changes is only implied, and only for extraction ('no writing selectors'). missing for 10: dedicated act/click/type primitives on described elements, documented DOM-understanding element resolution, evidence of surviving selector/layout changes, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can drive the page through DOM-understanding action primitives (act/click/type on described elements) that survive selector and layout changes

citations.quote: This enables you to break complex workflows into smaller, more reliable steps.
Your agent can navigate complex multi-step forms, handle dropdowns and checkboxes, and submit data
